Q: Passing 'va_list' as an argument to a variadic function A:

TL;DR: Although you can have use a va_list object in the variadic parameters of a function call, there is no portable way to retrieve the value of the original va_list because the object might have been converted to a different type that is incompatible with va_list. This is the case when va_list is implemented as an array type.

Passing a va_list * instead of a va_list allows the called function to modify the caller's va_list object with va_arg, or copy the caller's va_list object with va_copy, just by dereferencing the va_list * value.

Q: Tkinter Combobox bind <<ComboboxSelected>> causes KeyError: ' ' on initialization A:

The root of the problem is that bind requires you pass a function, not the result of calling a function (eg: self.calculate instead of self.calculate(...)). In your code, you are actually calling self.calculate when you define the bind rather than when the binding fires.

Since the values you are using are attributes on the object, you don't need to pass any values to the function.

First, pass the function and only the function to bind:

self.awg_comb.bind('<<ComboboxSelected>>', self.calculate)

Next, define your function such that it fetches the values if they aren't passed in. You also have to make sure to accept the event object that is passed in

    def calculate(self, event=None, dict_=None, key_=None):
        if dict_ is None:
            dict_ = self.awg_dict
        if key_ is None:
            key_ = self.sel_awg.get()

        self.val = dict_[key_]

        if dict_ == self.awg_dict:
            self.awg_uitk_label.configure(text = self.val)
        else:
            self.mm2_uitk_label.configure(text = self.val)

I don't understand when that final if statement would ever be false, but I left it in.

Q: In the Xero Journal entity, can the metadata or fields of Journal Lines be edited? A:

Generally speaking the journals themselves never get modified.

When a transaction is edited in Xero the following will occur:

  • A new journal is posted to reverse the original one.

  • A second new journal is posted to record the new values.

  • If a transaction is deleted or voided, then only the reversal journal is posted.

As such an invoice that has been edited once, will be recorded through three journals, the first two will however cancel each other out.
